task: Ocular accommodation: the Helmholtz mechanism -- ciliary contraction relaxes zonular tension, the elastic lens capsule rounds the lens, dioptric power increases. Model accommodative amplitude (diopters) as a function of lens/capsule elastic moduli and ciliary force; falsify by reproducing the measured ~10-14D young amplitude from lens-rounding geometry + capsule elasticity, and by reproducing the age-related collapse to <2D by ~52y via lens/capsule STIFFENING (not ciliary-muscle weakening) -- forcing the competing 'muscle weakens' hypothesis to its strongest test and showing it falls. Overshoot/inverse: a rigid-lens model must fail to accommodate at any age.
confidence_tier: literature-parameter-anchored geometric/optical model (verified schematic-eye radii cross-calibrated against this repo's own EYE-OPTICS-FORWARD-MODEL cell + measured lens/nucleus/cortex elastic-modulus and ciliary-muscle-MRI data) PLUS a literature-internal forced-adversary-resolved arc (Fisher 1971 -> Heys 2004 -> Weeber 2007) that is THEIR validated quantitative result, cited not reinvented. NOT a reprocessing of primary raw biometry/indentation data (unavailable for live fetch this session); NOT an independent re-derivation of Hofstetter's exact clinical-formula coefficients or Duane's original tabulated numbers (both flagged as open gaps, see symmetric_qc_open_items).

fisher_1971_global_elasticity.cite: Fisher RF (1971). The elastic constants of the human lens. J Physiol 212(1):147-180.

fisher_1971_global_elasticity.numbers: VERBATIM: 'Young's Modulus of Elasticity of the lens varies with age, polar elasticity and equatorial elasticity, at birth being 0.75 x 10(3) and 0.85 x 10(3) Nm(-2) respectively, while at 63 years of age both are equal to 3 x 10(3) Nm(-2)... the loss of accommodation due solely to an increase in Young's Modulus of Elasticity of the lens between the ages of 15 and 60. heys_cram_truscott_2004_regional_stiffne.cite: Heys KR, Cram SL, Truscott RJ (2004). Massive increase in the stiffness of the human lens nucleus with age: the basis for presbyopia? Mol Vis 10:956-963.

heys_cram_truscott_2004_regional_stiffne.numbers: VERBATIM: 'There was a pronounced increase in lens stiffness over the age range from 14 to 78. In the nucleus, stiffness values varied almost 1,000 fold over this age range... Nuclear stiffness values increased on average by a factor of 450. By contrast, in the cortex the average increase in stiffness was approximately 20 fold... In lenses younger than age 30, the nucleus was found to be softer than the cortex... In contrast all lenses older than 30 were characterized by having nuclear values higher than those of the cortex. In lenses over the age of 50, the lens nucleus was typically an order of magnitude more rigid than that of the cortex. The crossover age... was in the 30s... There was no significant change in the water content of the human lens nucleus from age 13 to age 82.' DECISIVE regional/gradient data -- the crossover (not just the magnitude) is the geometrically load-bearing fact used in this doc's mechanism (§2).

symmetric_qc_open_items: Hofstetter's exact clinical-formula coefficients (15-0.25*age etc.) are the standard, widely-reproduced convention, cross-validated here as 'the formula modern studies test against' (2 independent population studies), but NOT independently re-derived from Hofstetter 1965's primary text this session (no abstract available via efetch, pre-abstract-era record). The arithmetic match to the task's own '<2D by ~52' threshold is suggestive, not independent proof.

Duane 1922's original tabulated amplitude-vs-age numbers were NOT extracted this session: PMC's cloud viewer gates full-text/PDF access behind a client-side proof-of-work JS challenge for this pre-1975 scanned-page record, and Europe PMC's fullTextXML endpoint 404'd (not flagged open-access). Not fought (same class as a bot-blocked fetch). Existence/PMID/PMCID/journal/year verified live; content relied on Hofstetter's formula + modern replications instead.

A genuine, disclosed, PUBLISHED scientific disagreement exists on the exact nucleus/cortex stiffness-gradient crossover age and even some directional details across measurement methods: Weeber et al 2007 (PMID 17285335) report their old-lens finding as opposite in direction to 'earlier results described by Fisher (1971)... for lenses younger than 70-years-old', with a live comment/author-reply exchange (Schachar RA, PMID 17622549) on record -- not adjudicated by this doc.

Croft & Kaufman 1998's aging-rhesus-monkey data (PMID 9843878) show ciliary body movement amplitude AND velocity declining with age, with the authors' own language suggesting 'ciliary body dysfunction plays a role in presbyopia' -- a genuine complication for a clean 'muscle never changes' narrative. Resolved in this doc via Strenk 2010's explicit statement that human accommodative mechanics differ from the rhesus model, plus the movement-amplitude-vs-intrinsic-contractile-force distinction -- this is a reasoned inference from the cited papers, not a new independent measurement.

No capsule-specific (as distinct from whole-lens or nucleus/cortex) elastic-modulus-vs-age trend was independently verified this session. Fisher 1971's spinning-lens method measures a whole-lens (capsule+cortex+nucleus) response; the mechanism analysis instead relies on the nucleus/cortex-specific data (Heys 2004, Weeber 2007), which the field has most directly and quantitatively resolved.

The nucleus/cortex stiffness-gradient-reversal toy model (script STEP 6, a reciprocal-of-modulus construction fit to Heys 2004's own fold-change numbers) is ILLUSTRATIVE ONLY -- not independently validated against Duane's actual curve shape in this session. It is explicitly subordinated to Weeber & van der Heijde 2007's own validated, peer-reviewed mechanical model, which is the real quantitative anchor for the 'almost the entire loss' claim (G5).

Dubbelman 2005's exact reported mm/diopter radius-change coefficients and equivalent-index-rise magnitude were NOT extracted from the abstract text (only the DIRECTION of each effect is abstract-confirmed) -- the specific '<1.3% relative index rise' number in G1/STEP 3 is THIS document's own back-solved requirement to reconcile Gullstrand's classic paired radii with the classic 11.9D amplitude, cross-checked only for DIRECTION (not magnitude) against Dubbelman 2005's independently measured trend.

The Gullstrand accommodated radii pair (R1=5.33mm, R2=-5.33mm, t=4.5mm) and the classic '11.9D' amplitude figure are the standard textbook construct (Atchison & Smith, already used by this repo's own EYE-OPTICS-FORWARD-MODEL cell) -- not independently re-derived from Gullstrand's 1909 original (pre-PubMed, not eutils-verifiable) in this session.
